The paper presents a method to optimize the material properties of flexible blades for wind turbines.
The method uses a universal scaling approach based on two dimensionless parameters: the Cauchy number and the centrifugal number.
The Cauchy number represents the aerodynamic intensity compared to the restoring force of the torsion spring.
The centrifugal number represents the centrifugal intensity compared to the restoring force of the torsion spring.
The Blade Element Momentum (BEM) theory is used to study wind turbines aerodynamics.
The pitch angle distribution is optimized to maximize the efficiency of the turbine.
The optimal pitch angle distribution is found to be a decreasing function of the radius and the tip-speed ratio.
The optimization method reduces the problem to two dimensionless parameters, making it easier to apply to different wind turbine geometries.
The results show a significant increase in efficiency and harvested power, up to +35%, for a commercial wind turbine.
The method can be applied to any wind turbine geometry.
The Cauchy number and the centrifugal number are found to be scale-independent.
The pitch angle distribution is found to be sensitive to the Cauchy number and the centrifugal number.
The optimization method can be used to find the optimal material properties for flexible blades.
The results are validated using a commercial wind turbine geometry.
The method can be used to improve the efficiency and versatility of wind turbines.
